audience: Higgs 2026 conference: theorists and experimentalists from ATLAS/CMS/pheno, not CMS-internal; 15 min talk

1.description:
**1. Message.** This is the title slide. The bold blue title, "Constraints on Higgs-charm couplings at CMS", states the topic. There is no take-away line, which is normal for a title slide.

**2. Text.** The text is short: the title, the speaker name (Chirayu Gupta), "on behalf of the CMS Collaboration", the affiliation (Vrije Universiteit Brussel), and a line with the event, place and date ("Higgs 2026, Louvain-la-Neuve, 28 October 2026"). There are no undefined symbols. The only acronyms are CMS (in the title and the logo) and VUB (which appears only inside the logo, next to the full name). I see no grammar problems.

**3. Figures.** There are no plots. The only images are two logos at the bottom centre:
- the CMS logo, a detector cross-section with red tracks
- the VUB logo, the "VUB" mark next to "VRIJE UNIVERSITEIT BRUSSEL"

The CMS label, luminosity and energy questions don't apply because there are no data plots.

**4. Layout.**
- **Sizes:** The title is large. The name is medium sized. The collaboration and affiliation lines are smaller but still readable.
- **Contrast:** The event/date line is grey on white, so it has lower contrast than the black text.
- **Spacing:** Nothing overlaps or is cut off. A solid blue footer bar runs along the bottom edge.
- **Logo sizes:** The two logos are about the same height. The VUB block takes up more width.
- **Colour:** No meaning is carried by a red/green difference. The red tracks in the CMS logo are decoration only.

content.reason: Title slide. The title states the topic plainly, and the speaker, collaboration, affiliation, event, place and date are all there. No undefined symbols and nothing superfluous. A take-away is not expected on a title slide.

readability.reason: The title is large, nothing overlaps or is clipped, and the remaining text is readable. The event/date line is grey on white, so it has less contrast than the black text and may wash out on a projector. The two logos are about the same height but the VUB block is wider, which makes the logo row look slightly lopsided.

issues.description: The event/date line ('Higgs 2026, Louvain-la-Neuve, 28 October 2026') is grey on white and has lower contrast than the rest of the text, so it may wash out when projected.
issues.suggested_fix: Use dark grey (at least #444) or black for the event/date line, or make it slightly larger.

issues.description: The logos match in height, but the VUB block is wider than the CMS logo, so the bottom-centre logo row looks unbalanced.
issues.suggested_fix: Scale the logos to similar visual weight (for example, shrink the VUB block slightly or centre the pair with equal margins), or use the compact VUB mark without the long wordmark.

2.description:
## Slide 2/15: "Why the Higgs-charm coupling?"

**1. Message**
- The slide argues that the charm Yukawa coupling is the next open question after the third-generation fermions and the muon. The title only asks the question. The closest thing to a take-away is the last bullet, which is also a question: "Does the Higgs mechanism also give the 2nd-generation quarks their mass?" No declarative take-away line is given.
- "entering this region" is highlighted in orange.

**2. Text**
- There are five main bullets and two sub-bullets, filling the left half of the slide. The text is moderately dense, and the lines are mostly full sentences or clauses.
- Symbols and acronyms: κ_c is defined (κ_c = y_c/y_c^SM). y_c is not explicitly defined but is implied by the word "Yukawa". "SM" and "BSM" are not spelled out, and neither is "B(H → cc̄)". These are standard for this audience. The left column does not define "spontaneous flavour violation" beyond the example.
- Grammar: no errors. The phrase "couplings to t, b, τ and µ measured, all SM-like" is telegraphic but readable.

**3. Figure** (right half, one two-panel plot)
- **Upper panel:** coupling modifiers shown as κ_F·m_F/v or √κ_V·m_V/v (log scale, 10⁻⁴ to 10⁰) against particle mass. Points are shown for μ, c, τ, b, W, Z and t, with a red "SM prediction" line. The legend lists Observed, a star marker for arXiv:2509.22535 ("not part of combined fit"), 68% CL and 95% CL (stat ⊕ syst), and SM prediction. Annotations read "All κ_i ≥ 0", m_H = 125.38 GeV and p_SM = 0.12. There is a particle-table inset (leptons, quarks, force carriers, Higgs boson) with colour-coded cells.
- **Lower panel:** "Ratio to SM" (0.5 to 1.5) against "Particle mass (GeV)" (log scale, ~10⁻¹ to ~3×10²). A small inset zooms to 0.9 to 1.1 for W, Z and t. At the charm mass there is a grey vertical line spanning the full ratio range, with a downward arrow at the bottom.
- **Label:** "CMS Supplementary", 138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV).
- **Units:** GeV appears on the x axis. The y quantities are dimensionless.
- **Caption:** "CMS, Rep. Prog. Phys. 89 (2026) 087801 (supplementary)". This is a citation only and makes no claim.
- **Text vs. plot:** the bullet "|κ_c| ∼ 3: current sensitivity is entering this region" is not directly shown. The ratio axis stops at 1.5, and the charm result appears only as a grey line or limit, with no κ_c ≈ 3 mark.
- **Size:** the plot takes about 35% of the slide width. The legend text, annotations and particle-table labels are very small and probably can't be read when projected. The axis tick labels are small but legible.

**4. Layout**
- There is no overlap or clipping.
- Font sizes inside the figure (legend, inset, the "not part of combined fit" note) are very small.
- The orange highlighted phrase on white has moderate contrast.
- The plot uses orange, purple, blue and grey markers with a red SM line. No distinction relies on red and green alone.
- The footer (author, title, conference, page number 2/15) is small but legible.

content.reason: The motivation is clear: third-generation and muon couplings are measured and SM-like, and charm is the next open case. But the slide ends on a question, with no declarative take-away. The key bullet '|κ_c| ∼ 3: current sensitivity is entering this region' is not shown in the figure, because the ratio axis stops at 1.5 and charm appears only as a grey line with an arrow. 'Spontaneous flavour violation' is used without a definition. The figure has to be explained aloud for the audience to see why charm stands out.

readability.reason: The plot is the main evidence, yet it takes only about 35% of the slide width. Its legend, annotations (p_SM, m_H, 'not part of combined fit') and the particle-table inset are too small to read when projected. The text column takes the larger share of the slide and competes with the figure. Axis ticks can be read, but the charm limit, which is the point of the slide, is a thin grey line that is hard to spot.

issues.description: The bullet's claim that sensitivity is reaching |κ_c| ∼ 3 is not shown in the figure. The ratio panel stops at 1.5 and charm is just a grey line with an arrow and no number.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an annotation or callout at the charm point giving the current observed and expected |κ_c| limits with a citation, or put the number in the text with its source (for example the CMS VH(cc) or combination result).

issues.description: The figure's legend, annotations and particle-table inset are too small to read when projected, and the figure is too small for its role.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the plot about 55-60% of the slide width. Crop or drop the particle-table inset and the lower-panel zoom inset if they can't be enlarged, and cut the text to make room.

issues.description: There is no declarative take-away. The title and the last bullet are both questions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a statement at the bottom, for example: 'Charm is the heaviest fermion whose Higgs coupling is still unmeasured: current limits |κ_c| ≲ 3, SM is κ_c = 1.'

issues.description: 'Spontaneous flavour violation' appears without a definition or reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short parenthetical (for example 'BSM models where light-quark Yukawas are enhanced without FCNC') and a reference, or drop it.

issues.description: The text is moderately wordy, with five bullets and two sub-bullets in full clauses.
issues.suggested_fix: Cut to three short bullets: what's measured (t, b, τ, μ SM-like), what's open (2nd-generation quarks), where charm stands (|κ_c| limit vs SM).

issues.description: The orange highlight on white has only moderate contrast.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a darker orange or bold black for the highlighted phrase.

issues.description: The charm result in the lower panel is a grey line that blends into the background.
issues.suggested_fix: Draw it in a strong colour with a label (for example 'κ_c limit, off scale ↓') so the audience's eye goes to it.

3.description:
**1. Message**

The slide is an overview of the four ways CMS constrains κ_c: direct H→cc̄, H+charm production, indirect constraints from Higgs rates and width, and rare exclusive decays. Each route has its key publications and headline limit. The title "How CMS probes κ_c" gives the topic but not a conclusion. No take-away line says which route is strongest or how the routes compare. You can only infer that from the numbers: |κ_c| < 3.5 for direct, < 47 for cH, and −166 < κ_c < 208 for rare decays.

**2. Text**

- **Amount:** moderate and dense. There are four boxes, each with 2 to 4 lines plus journal references, and two footer lines below.
- **Symbols defined in the footer:** μ, Γ_H, and the obs. (exp.) convention.
- **μ:** it is defined in the footer but never appears anywhere else on the slide.
- **κ_c:** not defined on this slide.
- **Undefined labels and acronyms:**
  - "γH paper" is an internal label the audience may not know.
  - VH, tt̄H, ggH and cg → cH are not expanded. These are standard for the audience.
  - "comb." is an abbreviation.
- **Vague wording:**
  - "κ_c ∈ [−3.3, 2.8] to [−8.6, 7.5] (by assumptions)" doesn't say which assumptions give which range.
  - "Run 3 delivered the tools (slide 13)" is vague.
- **Inconsistencies:**
  - The rare-decay limit (−166 < κ_c < 208) and the indirect intervals don't say whether they are observed or expected, unlike the "best:" lines in the top boxes.
  - Notation spacing varies a little: "H → cc̄" versus "H→4ℓ" and "H→J/ψγ".
- **Grammar:** no grammar errors. The text is in note style rather than full sentences.

**3. Figures**

- The slide has no plots or figures. The only graphic is the CMS logo in the top right.
- No CMS or luminosity label applies. The footer gives the dataset as Run 2, 13 TeV, 138 fb⁻¹.

**4. Layout**

- **Grid:** a 2×2 grid of rounded, light-blue boxes with dark-blue bold headers, on a white background with a dark-blue title bar.
- **Small text:**
  - The journal references (e.g. "PRL 131 (2023) 061801", "arXiv:2607.23352") are set in a very small font, much smaller than the body text. They are probably hard to read when projected.
  - The slide pointers ("slides 4–7", "slide 11") are small and grey, so contrast is lower but still readable.
- **"NEW" tags:** orange, small, appearing in the indirect box and the footer.
- **Spacing:** the boxes have some empty space on the right and bottom, especially the top-right and bottom-right boxes. No text overlaps or is clipped.
- **Colour:** no distinctions rely on red versus green.
- **Footer:** the author, talk title, conference and the page number 3/15 are in a small grey footer.

content.reason: The topic (four CMS routes to κ_c) is clear, and each route has a headline limit. But the title only names the topic, and no take-away says that direct H→cc̄ gives the strongest bound or how the routes compare, so the audience has to work this out from scattered numbers. There are also several loose ends: the indirect κ_c range is given 'by assumptions' without saying which assumption gives which range, the rare-decay and indirect limits don't say whether they are observed or expected, 'γH paper' is an internal label, κ_c is not defined on the slide, and μ is defined in the footer but never used.

readability.reason: The 2×2 box layout is clean and the body text is readable, with nothing clipped or overlapping. However, the journal references are in a very small font that won't read when projected, the grey slide pointers have low contrast, and the slide is text-only and dense. The empty space in the right-hand boxes could have gone to larger text.

issues.description: No take-away. The title names the topic but gives no conclusion, and nothing compares the routes or says which is strongest.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the title a conclusion, e.g. 'Direct H→cc̄ gives the tightest κ_c bound (|κ_c|<3.5); cH and rare decays are complementary', or add a one-line take-away box under the grid.

issues.description: The indirect range 'κ_c ∈ [−3.3, 2.8] to [−8.6, 7.5] (by assumptions)' doesn't say which assumption gives which interval.
issues.suggested_fix: Give the assumption for each end, e.g. '[−3.3, 2.8] (B_inv=B_undet=0) … [−8.6, 7.5] (Γ_H from off-shell)', or quote a single representative interval and name its assumption.

issues.description: Limits are reported inconsistently. The top boxes give 'best: obs. (exp.)', but the rare-decay limit (−166<κ_c<208) and the indirect intervals don't say whether they are observed or expected.
issues.suggested_fix: Label every limit as obs. (exp.) in the same format, with the CL (95%).

issues.description: 'γH paper' is an internal label the external audience won't know.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace it with the physics name (e.g. 'H+γ production' or 'H→J/ψγ, Υγ search') and the journal reference.

issues.description: κ_c is not defined on this slide, and μ is defined in the footer but never used.
issues.suggested_fix: Add 'κ_c = y_c/y_c^SM' once (e.g. in the title bar or footer) and drop the unused μ definition.

issues.description: The journal references are in a very small font that won't read from the back of the room.
issues.suggested_fix: Raise them to at least about 60% of the body size, or move the full references to a backup slide and keep a short tag (e.g. 'PRL 2023').

issues.description: 'Run 3 delivered the tools (slide 13)' is vague.
issues.suggested_fix: Name the tools concretely (e.g. 'new ParticleNet c-tagging, displaced-vertex triggers → slide 13') or drop the line.

issues.description: The grey slide pointers have low contrast, and the orange 'NEW' tags are small.
issues.suggested_fix: Use dark grey or the body colour for the pointers. Keep the 'NEW' tags but slightly larger, or drop them if the take-away line covers what is new.

issues.description: Notation spacing is inconsistent ('H → cc̄' vs 'H→4ℓ', 'H→J/ψγ'), and 'comb.' is abbreviated.
issues.suggested_fix: Use one arrow spacing throughout and spell out 'combination'.

issues.description: There is unused white space in the right-hand boxes while the text is dense elsewhere.
issues.suggested_fix: Enlarge the body font to fill the boxes, or add a small summary graphic (e.g. a horizontal bar chart of the four κ_c intervals on one axis).

4.description:
## Slide 4/15: "Direct H → cc̄: VH(H → cc̄)"

The text layer drops the overbars and cuts off partway through. The image shows them as cc̄, so I use cc̄ below. Text that the layer cuts off is read from the image.

**1. Message**
- The main point is stated in a blue take-away line at the bottom: "The most sensitive single channel of Run 2 (expected μ < 7.6)".
- There are two side points. VZ(Z→cc̄) is observed at 5.7σ, which "validates the method". The observed limit excludes κ_c = 1 because of an upward fluctuation (μ̂ = 7.7), with a pointer to backup.

**2. Text**
- There is a moderate amount of text: three bullets on the left, a results box ("VH(H → cc̄)") under them, a caption under each plot, the take-away line, and a reference in the top right ("PRL 131 (2023) 061801, CMS-HIG-21-008").
- The bullets are terse fragments: "Leptonic W/Z decays: 0, 1, 2 leptons"; "Resolved (two small-radius c jets) and merged-jet (one large-radius jet) topologies; ParticleNet c tagging"; "VZ(Z→ cc̄) observed at 5.7σ: validates the method".
- The box reads: "95% CL obs. (exp.)", "μ < 14 (7.6)", "1.1 < |κ_c| < 5.5 (< 3.4)", "obs. excludes κ_c = 1: upward fluctuation, μ̂ = 7.7 → backup".
- Symbols and terms not defined on the slide:
  - μ (signal strength), κ_c and μ̂
  - "ParticleNet"
  - S/(S+B)
  - the row labels 0L/1L/2L in the right plot (the first bullet implies they mean lepton counts)
- No grammar errors. The text is written in note style, without full sentences.

**3. Figures**
- **Left plot:**
  - It shows the Higgs candidate mass in the merged-jet topology, all categories, with events weighted by S/(S+B).
  - x axis: "Higgs boson candidate mass [GeV]", 60–200. y axis: "S/(S+B) weighted events", 0–1000.
  - Main panel: observed data points over stacked backgrounds. The legend has 12 entries, including Z+jets, W+jets, tt̄, single top, VV(other), VZ(Z→bb̄), VZ(Z→cc̄), VH(H→bb̄), B uncertainty, and VH(H→cc̄) with μ = 7.7.
  - Lower panel: "B subtracted", y range −50 to 100. It shows the VZ(Z→cc̄) peak (grey) near 90 GeV and the VH(H→cc̄) signal (red) near 125 GeV.
  - Label: "CMS" with no Preliminary tag, plus "138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV)".
  - The caption, "Merged-jet m(H_cand), events weighted by S/(S+B)", matches what the plot shows.
- **Right plot:**
  - It shows 95% CL upper limits on μ_VH(H→cc̄), x axis 0–40.
  - Six rows: Combined, Merged-jet, Resolved-jet, 0L, 1L, 2L.
  - Each row shows the observed limit (solid line), the median expected limit (dashed line), and 68% (green) and 95% (yellow) expected bands.
  - Each row label prints its numbers. Combined is exp 7.60 / obs 14.4, Merged-jet 8.75 / 16.9, and Resolved-jet 19.0 / 13.9. From the image, 0L reads about 12.6 / 18.3, 1L 11.5 / 19.1 and 2L 14.3 / 20.4.
  - Label: "CMS", "138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV)".
  - The caption is "μ limits per channel". The box value μ < 14 (7.6) matches the Combined row (14.4 / 7.60).
- **Size:** Each plot takes up about a third of the slide width. Legend entries, tick labels and the per-row numbers in the right plot are very small and would be hard to read when projected.

**4. Layout**
- There is no overlap or clipping.
- The box text and captions are smaller than the bullets but readable. The text inside both plots is the smallest on the slide.
- Contrast is fine: black or white on light backgrounds, and white on the blue title bar and box header.
- The limit bands use green and yellow, not red and green. In the left stack, the red signal fill and the pink VV(other) fill are similar in hue. The legend's colour swatches are tiny.

content.reason: The main message is stated in the take-away line: the most sensitive Run 2 channel, expected μ < 7.6. The Combined row of the limit plot backs it up, and the box numbers match it (14.4 / 7.60). The two side points (VZ at 5.7σ as validation, and the observed exclusion of κ_c = 1 from an upward fluctuation) are useful but split attention across three messages. Minor gaps: S/(S+B) and μ̂ are not defined, 0L/1L/2L is only implied, and 'single channel' is ambiguous (single analysis vs single production mode).

readability.reason: The bullets and the results box are readable. Each plot takes only about a third of the slide width, and they compete with the text. The legend in the left plot has 12 tiny entries with very small swatches. The per-row numbers and tick labels in the right plot will not read when projected. The red signal and pink VV(other) fills look alike. The box repeats the key numbers, so the problem is not a blocker, but the figures are too small for how much they matter.

issues.description: Both plots are about a third of the slide width. The legend entries, tick labels and per-row limit values on the right are unreadable from the back of the room.
issues.suggested_fix: Shrink the bullets to two short lines and let the plots fill about 80% of the width. Or keep only the limit-summary plot at large size and move the S/(S+B) mass plot to backup.

issues.description: There are three messages on one slide: the sensitivity take-away, VZ validation at 5.7σ, and the observed exclusion of κ_c = 1 with μ̂ = 7.7.
issues.suggested_fix: Keep the take-away as the headline. Put VZ validation in one short phrase. Shorten the fluctuation note to '(obs. > exp.: μ̂ = 7.7, see backup)'.

issues.description: S/(S+B) weighting and μ̂ are not defined. The meaning of 0L/1L/2L in the right plot is only implied by the first bullet.
issues.suggested_fix: In the caption, write 'events weighted by expected S/(S+B) per category'. Change the bullet to '0L/1L/2L: Z→νν, W→ℓν, Z→ℓℓ'. Write 'best-fit μ̂ = 7.7'.

issues.description: 'The most sensitive single channel of Run 2' is ambiguous: it could mean among H→cc̄ searches, among VH searches, or across experiments. A mixed ATLAS/CMS/pheno audience will notice the ambiguity.
issues.suggested_fix: Make it specific, for example: 'Most sensitive direct H→cc̄ search of Run 2 (exp. μ < 7.6)'.

issues.description: The red VH(H→cc̄) signal fill and the pink VV(other) fill look alike in the stack, and the legend swatches are tiny.
issues.suggested_fix: Label the signal directly in the B-subtracted panel ('VH(H→cc̄), μ = 7.7' next to the red peak, 'VZ(Z→cc̄)' next to the grey one) so nobody has to rely on the legend.

5.description:
The slide is titled "Direct H → cc̄: boosted H" (slide 5/15). It cites PRL 131 (2023) 041801 and CMS-HIG-21-012 at the upper right.

**1. Message**
- The main point is that the boosted H → cc̄ search is an independent, high-pT constraint dominated by ggH.
- This is stated in a bold blue take-away line at the bottom: "An independent, high-p_T handle dominated by ggH".
- A boxed result, "Boosted H → cc̄: μ < 47 (39) 95% CL", is the headline number.
- A second point is that Z → cc̄ was observed in Z+jets at high pT, with μ_Z quoted.

**2. Text**
- There are three bullets on the left in short, clipped phrases:
  - "p_T^H > 450 GeV, mostly ggH; H → cc̄ in one large-radius jet"
  - "Double-charm DNN tagger (DeepDoubleX); jet-mass fit"
  - "**Z→ cc̄ observed** in Z+jets at high p_T, first time: μ_Z = 1.00 +0.17/−0.14 (syst), > 5σ"
- The plot caption reads: "Jet mass in the c-tag passing (left) and failing (right) regions; the peak is Z→ cc̄".
- Undefined on the slide:
  - ggH, DNN and DeepDoubleX are not expanded.
  - μ is not defined as a signal strength.
  - The "(39)" in "μ < 47 (39)" is not labelled as the expected limit.
  - Plot labels σ_Data and m_SD are not defined.
- The μ_Z uncertainty is labelled "(syst)" only. No statistical or theory component is shown.
- The bullets use telegraphic grammar (semicolons, "first time:"), but nothing is outright ungrammatical.

**3. Figures**
There are two side-by-side published CMS plots. Both carry the "CMS" label (no "Preliminary"), "138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV)", "450 < p_T < 1200 GeV" and "DeepDoubleX".
- **Left (Passing Region):**
  - Stacked histogram of Events / 7 GeV against "Jet m_SD [GeV]", from 40 to 200 GeV, with y up to about 1.2×10⁴.
  - A visible red Z(cc̄) peak and green W components sit around 80 to 100 GeV.
  - The H(cc̄)×200 signal is shown as a dashed blue line.
- **Right (Failing Region):**
  - Same axes, with y up to about 2×10⁶.
  - A smoothly falling, QCD-dominated distribution; the resonant components are barely visible in the upper panel.
- **Both plots:**
  - The legend lists Data, Z(cc̄), Z(bb̄), Z(qq̄), W(cq̄), W(qq̄), H(bb̄), H(cc̄), Other, QCD and H(cc̄)×200.
  - Both show μ_Z(cc) = 1.0 and μ_H(cc) = 9.4.
  - A lower panel shows (Data − Bkg)/σ_Data with a grey "Bkg. unc." band, and the residual peak near 90 GeV is visible there.
- **Caption accuracy:** The caption's "the peak is Z→ cc̄" fits the left upper panel and both residual panels. In the right upper panel, no peak can be seen.
- **Size:** Each plot is about a quarter of the slide width. Legends, the μ annotations, tick labels and the residual-panel axis labels are very small and probably not readable when projected.

**4. Layout**
- The plot-internal text is the smallest on the slide. The caption is also in a small font.
- There is no overlap or clipping.
- Contrast is fine: dark text on white, white text on the blue title bar and the result box.
- In the stack, red Z(cc̄) sits next to dark-green W(cq̄) and light-green W(qq̄), so some components are told apart only by red versus green.
- The footer reads "C. Gupta | Constraints on Higgs-charm couplings | Higgs 2026 5/15", and the CMS logo is at the upper right.

content.reason: The take-away is stated and the boxed limit μ < 47 (39) matches PRL 131 (2023) 041801. But the slide carries two messages: the H limit in the headline and the Z→cc̄ observation in the figure. The plots support the Z calibration, not the H constraint or the 'dominated by ggH' claim, and the slide never connects the two. The audience needs several things that are not defined: μ as signal strength, (39) as the expected limit, the μ_H(cc) = 9.4 printed on the plots, m_SD, σ_Data and DeepDoubleX. μ_Z is labelled '(syst)' only, while the paper also quotes stat and theory components, so the uncertainty looks incomplete.

readability.reason: The figure is the dominant evidence, but each plot is only about a quarter of the slide width. Legends, μ annotations, tick labels and residual-panel axis labels will not be readable from the back of the room. The failing-region plot shows no visible resonance in its upper panel, so it takes space without adding to the message. The caption is in a small font, and the stack separates Z(cc̄) from W(cq̄)/W(qq̄) only by red versus green.

issues.description: Plots are about a quarter of the slide width each. Legend, μ annotations, axis labels and residual panels are unreadable when projected.
issues.suggested_fix: Drop the failing-region plot and show only the passing region at about half the slide width or more. Shorten the bullets to make room.

issues.description: The figure shows the Z→cc̄ calibration peak, but the headline and take-away are about the H→cc̄ limit. The link between them (Z peak validates the tagger and mass fit) is not stated.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one line such as 'Z→cc̄ peak (μ_Z = 1.00) validates the tagger and the m_SD fit', or make the caption say this explicitly.

issues.description: μ_Z = 1.00 +0.17/−0.14 is labelled '(syst)' only. The paper also quotes theory (±0.08) and stat (±0.06) components, so the slide makes the uncertainty look incomplete or mislabelled.
issues.suggested_fix: Quote all components as in the PRL, or give the total uncertainty without the '(syst)' label.

issues.description: 'μ < 47 (39)' does not mark which number is observed and which expected, and μ is not defined as a signal strength relative to the SM.
issues.suggested_fix: Write 'μ_H < 47 obs. (39 exp.) at 95% CL, μ = σ×B / SM'.

issues.description: μ_H(cc) = 9.4 is printed on the plots with no explanation and could be read as a measurement or as tension.
issues.suggested_fix: Mention it in the caption as the best-fit value, consistent with SM within the limit, or crop it out.

issues.description: m_SD, σ_Data, DeepDoubleX and ggH are not defined for a non-CMS audience.
issues.suggested_fix: Caption: 'soft-drop jet mass'. Bullet: 'double-charm jet tagger (DNN)'. Expand ggH once on an earlier slide.

issues.description: The 'the peak is Z→cc̄' caption also covers the failing-region upper panel, where no peak is visible.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolved by dropping the failing plot. Otherwise reword it to 'peak in the passing region'.

issues.description: The 'mostly ggH' claim is not supported by anything on the slide.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the approximate ggH fraction at pT > 450 GeV from the paper, or soften it to 'ggH-dominated production'.

issues.description: Z(cc̄) and the W components are separated only by red versus green, which is hard for colour-vision-deficient viewers.
issues.suggested_fix: Accept it since it is the published figure, but point to the Z peak with an arrow or label on the slide.

6.description:
**1. Message**

The slide presents ttH(H→cc̄) as a new channel and gives its limits. The title says "a new channel". A blue take-away line at the bottom says: "A second direct channel, with expected sensitivity comparable to VH". The slide shows no VH numbers, so the VH comparison is not supported by anything on this page.

**2. Text**

- **Left column:** four bullets of moderate length:
  - 0, 1 and 2-lepton tt̄ decays with many jets of all flavours.
  - Jets in b/c/light **2D tagging categories** (ParticleNet), plus a transformer event classifier (ParT).
  - A **simultaneous** fit of tt̄H(cc̄), tt̄H(bb̄) and tt̄Z, with tt̄+cc̄/bb̄ taken from control regions.
  - A check with tt̄Z(Z→cc̄): μ = 1.0 ± 0.8, with a pointer "→ backup".
- **Centre box:** a summary of results, "95% CL obs. (exp.)": μ < 7.8 (8.7); |κc| < 3.0 (3.3) with κb = 1; |κc| < 4.2 obs. with κb fitted.
- **Undefined terms:** μ (signal strength), κc and κb are not defined on the slide. "tt̄+cc̄/bb̄" is jargon. ParT is only given as a parenthetical after "transformer event classifier".
- **Grammar:** no grammar problems are visible.
- **Reference:** "PRL 136 (2026) 011801, CMS-HIG-24-018" at top right.

**3. Figures**

- **Centre plot (limits per channel):**
  - It shows horizontal bars of the 95% CL upper limit on μ_tt̄H(cc̄) for four rows: All, 0L, 1L and 2L.
  - Each row has small "Exp./Obs." numbers. The text layer gives All 8.7/7.8, 0L 13/14 and 1L Exp. 12. The image appears to show 1L Obs. 6.6 and 2L 23/35, but these numbers are very small.
  - The x-axis runs from 0 to 50 and is labelled with the upper limit on μ. The y-axis has category labels only.
  - The legend shows Observed, Median expected, 68% expected (yellow) and 95% expected (blue).
  - It carries a "CMS" label and "138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV)". A red vertical line sits near μ = 1 and is not labelled.
  - The caption reads "μ_tt̄H(cc̄) limits per channel". The plot is small, and the per-row numbers and the axis title would be hard to read when projected.
- **Right plot (likelihood scan):**
  - It shows −2Δln L against |κc| from 0 to 7. Red curves are κb fixed and blue curves are κb floating; solid lines are observed and dashed lines are expected.
  - Dotted horizontal reference lines sit at about 1 and 3.84. Neither is labelled.
  - The in-plot legend repeats the limits "|κc| < 3.0 @95% CL" and "< 4.2 @95% CL" in very small text.
  - It carries "CMS Supplementary" and "138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV)".
  - The caption reads "−2Δ ln L vs. |κc|, κb fixed or fitted from tt̄H(bb̄)". The plot itself only says "κb float." and does not show that κb comes from tt̄H(bb̄).

**4. Layout**

- The legend text and per-category numbers in both plots are very small. The body text is readable.
- Nothing overlaps or is clipped.
- Colours: the limit plot uses yellow and blue, and the scan uses red and blue. Nothing depends on telling red from green.
- The grey expected values in the centre box are in lower contrast than the black observed values.
- The footer reads "C. Gupta | Constraints on Higgs-charm couplings | Higgs 2026 | 6/15".

content.reason: The headline message (ttH(cc) gives a second direct κc channel with μ < 7.8 (8.7 exp.) and |κc| < 3.0) comes through and the figures and box back it up. The take-away line, though, claims sensitivity 'comparable to VH' and the slide shows no VH number at all, so its main comparative claim has nothing on the page behind it. μ, κc and κb are never defined, which matters for a mixed theory/experiment audience. 'tt̄+cc̄/bb̄' and ParT are jargon. The red line at μ = 1 in the limit plot and the 1 and 3.84 reference lines in the scan are unlabelled. The caption says κb comes from tt̄H(bb̄), but the plot only says 'κb float.'. The four left bullets plus a numbers box plus two plots is a lot for one slide in a 15-minute talk.

readability.reason: Body text is readable. The two figures carry the result, and in both the key content is too small to read when projected. In the limit plot, the per-row Exp./Obs. numbers and the axis title are tiny (the 1L/2L values can barely be made out). In the scan, the in-plot legend with the limits is very small. Both plots sit small next to three blocks of text, so text competes with the figures. The grey expected values in the centre box have low contrast. Nothing is clipped or overlapping, and the colour choices are safe.

issues.description: The take-away claims 'expected sensitivity comparable to VH', but no VH limit appears on the slide.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the VH(cc) expected limit next to it (e.g. 'VH: μ < X exp., |κc| < Y'), or change the wording to a claim the slide supports, e.g. 'A second, independent direct handle on κc'.

issues.description: Per-category numbers and the axis title in the μ limit plot are too small to read when projected.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the limit plot bigger (take space from the bullets) or crop it to the 'All' row plus channel bars. Put the key numbers in large text beside it rather than relying on the in-plot labels.

issues.description: μ, κc and κb are not defined, and the audience includes theorists and ATLAS people who may not know the CMS conventions.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one short line: 'μ = σ/σ_SM; κc, κb = coupling modifiers (κ = 1 is SM)'.

issues.description: The red vertical line at μ = 1 (limit plot) and the dotted lines at 1 and 3.84 (scan) are not labelled.
issues.suggested_fix: Annotate them as 'SM (μ=1)' and '68% / 95% CL'.

issues.description: The scan caption says κb comes from tt̄H(bb̄), but the plot only says 'κb float.', and the in-plot limit text is tiny.
issues.suggested_fix: Overlay a larger label, 'κb fitted (from tt̄H(bb̄))', on the blue curve and rely on the centre box for the numbers.

issues.description: There is too much text for a 15-minute slot: four bullets plus a results box plus two plots, and the box repeats limits already shown in the scan legend.
issues.suggested_fix: Cut the bullets to two (categories with ParticleNet/ParT tagging, and a simultaneous fit with tt̄+HF control regions). Keep only the obs. (exp.) box as the single place the numbers appear.

issues.description: The grey expected values in the results box have low contrast.
issues.suggested_fix: Use black or dark grey for the expected values, with brackets or a lighter weight to tell them apart.

issues.description: Jargon: 'tt̄+cc̄/bb̄' and 'ParT' are not explained.
issues.suggested_fix: Write 'tt̄ + extra c/b jets (main background, constrained in control regions)' and 'transformer classifier (Particle Transformer)'.

7.description:
**Slide 7/15: "Combination of tt̄H and VH: most stringent *direct* constraint on κc"**

**1. Message**
- The title states the point: the tt̄H + VH combination gives the most stringent direct constraint on κc.
- A blue bold line at the bottom gives a narrower take-away: "Best expected sensitivity to date, |κc| < 2.7: below the BSM-motivated |κc| ∼ 3".
- The title and the second bullet don't fully match. The title says the combination is the most stringent constraint. The second bullet and the right plot's legend show that tt̄H alone gives a tighter observed bound (|κc| < 3.0) than the combination (|κc| < 3.5). Only the bottom line limits the claim to *expected* sensitivity.

**2. Text**
- There is a moderate amount of text: a title, two bullets, a summary box and a take-away line. Each is one line.
- Summary box: header "tt̄H + VH", then "95% CL obs. (exp.)", "μH→cc̄ < 9.3 (5.6)", "|κc| < 3.5 (2.7)" and "SM production, κb = 1".
- Symbols not defined on the slide: μ̂ (best-fit signal strength), κb, and μ (only implied as the signal strength).
- Acronyms used without definition: CL, SM, BSM. These are standard for this audience.
- The "BSM-motivated |κc| ∼ 3" figure has no citation.
- The second bullet's "(3.0)" and "(3.5)" are |κc| values, but the bullet doesn't say so.
- The bullet numbers match the left plot: (7.6 − 5.6)/7.6 ≈ 26% and (8.7 − 5.6)/8.7 ≈ 36%.
- The VH best-fit value μ̂ = 7.7 is in the text only. Neither plot shows it.
- No grammar problems.
- The source is given as "PRL 136 (2026) 011801, CMS-HIG-24-018" above the right plot.

**3. Figures**
- **Left plot (limit summary):**
  - Shows 95% CL upper limits on μH→cc̄ for three rows: Combined (Exp. 5.6, Obs. 9.3), tt̄H(H→cc̄) (Exp. 8.7, Obs. 7.8) and VH(H→cc̄) (Exp. 7.6, Obs. 14).
  - Each row has a black observed marker, a dashed median-expected line, and yellow (68%) and blue (95%) bands.
  - A red vertical line at μ = 1 marks the SM value but has no legend entry.
  - X-axis: "95% CL upper limit on μH→cc̄", running 0 to 17.5. It has no units, which is correct for μ.
  - Label: "CMS Supplementary", 138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV).
  - The row labels and Exp./Obs. numbers are small.
- **Right plot (likelihood scan):**
  - Shows −2Δln(L) against |κc| from 0 to 3.5 for tt̄H (red), VH (blue) and the combination (black).
  - Observed curves are solid and expected curves are dashed. Markers show the best-fit points.
  - Horizontal dotted lines at about 1 and 3.84 mark the 68% and 95% CL levels. They aren't labelled.
  - The legend includes "|κc|obs tt̄H(H→cc̄) < 3.0 @95% CL" and "|κc|obs Comb. < 3.5 @95% CL".
  - Label: "CMS Supplementary", 138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV).
  - The legend and the y-axis title are very small, too small to read when projected.
  - The plot takes up about a third of the slide width.

**4. Layout**
- The two plots sit side by side, with the summary box to the right and the bullets and take-away below. Nothing overlaps or is clipped.
- The expected values in the summary box, "(5.6)" and "(2.7)", are in light grey, which has lower contrast than the black text.
- The plots separate curves by red, blue and black and by solid versus dashed lines. Nothing relies on red against green. The dashed and solid lines are thin and hard to tell apart at this size.
- The footer text is small but conventional.

content.reason: The title says the ttH+VH combination is the most stringent direct constraint on kappa_c, but the slide's own right plot and second bullet show ttH alone gives the tighter observed bound (|kappa_c| < 3.0 vs 3.5 combined). Only the bottom take-away limits the claim to expected sensitivity (2.7), and a non-CMS audience reading the title against the legend sees a contradiction. There are also unsupported or undefined items: the BSM-motivated |kappa_c| ~ 3 has no citation, mu-hat and kappa_b are undefined, the bare (3.0)/(3.5) in the bullet are not labelled as |kappa_c|, and the VH best fit of 7.7 appears in no figure.

readability.reason: The right plot carries the headline number but takes only about a third of the slide width. Its legend (which is where the 3.0 and 3.5 values appear) and its y-axis title cannot be read when projected. The left plot's row labels and Exp./Obs. numbers are small. The thin dashed and solid lines are hard to tell apart at this size. The expected values in the summary box are light grey and low contrast. Two plots, a summary box, two bullets and a take-away line all compete for space.

issues.description: The title says the combination is the most stringent constraint, but the observed ttH-only bound (|kappa_c| < 3.0) is tighter than the combined one (< 3.5), which the slide itself shows in the bullet and the right-plot legend.
issues.suggested_fix: Retitle to something like 'ttH + VH combination: best expected direct sensitivity to kappa_c (|kappa_c| < 2.7 exp.)'. Add one clause explaining that the observed combined limit (3.5) is weaker than ttH alone (3.0) because VH has an upward fluctuation (mu-hat = 7.7).

issues.description: The legend and y-axis title of the right likelihood-scan plot are unreadable when projected, and the plot is only about a third of the slide width even though it holds the key result.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the kappa_c scan the dominant figure, at least half the slide width. Move the mu limit summary to backup, or shrink it and take its numbers out of the bullets. Alternatively, restate the plot's legend numbers in large text next to it.

issues.description: The 'BSM-motivated |kappa_c| ~ 3' benchmark has no citation, yet the take-away depends on it.
issues.suggested_fix: Cite the model or paper behind the ~3 benchmark (for example, a small reference under the take-away line), or reword to a sourced statement.

issues.description: The second bullet's (3.0) and (3.5) are not labelled as |kappa_c| values, and the VH mu-hat = 7.7 is in the text but in neither plot.
issues.suggested_fix: Write '|kappa_c| < 3.0 (ttH) vs < 3.5 (comb.) observed' and define mu-hat as the best-fit signal strength.

issues.description: kappa_b = 1 and mu are not defined, and the red mu = 1 line in the left plot has no legend entry.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short footnote: 'mu = sigma x B / SM; kappa_b fixed to 1'. Label the red line 'SM'.

issues.description: The horizontal 68%/95% CL lines in the right plot are not labelled.
issues.suggested_fix: Add '68%' and '95%' text at the right edge of the dotted lines.

issues.description: The expected values in the summary box are light grey and low contrast.
issues.suggested_fix: Use black or dark grey for the expected values. Mark them with parentheses or italics instead of a lighter colour.

issues.description: The thin solid (observed) and dashed (expected) lines are hard to tell apart at projection size.
issues.suggested_fix: Use thicker lines in the re-made figure, or add a note on the slide: 'solid = observed, dashed = expected'.

8.description:
1. **Message.** The slide is about using H+c production to probe κc, with κc entering at the production vertex rather than through the H→cc̄ decay. The title ("H + charm production: κc in production") and the first bullet both say this. There is no separate take-away line.

2. **Text.**
   - There are four bullets, about 2 to 3 lines each, plus a reference line (JHEP 11 (2025) 060, CMS-HIG-23-010) and a caption. The text fills most of the top half of the slide.
   - Bullet 2, "σcH = 90 fb: σB ≈ 0.2 fb (γγ), ≈ 20 fb (WW)", uses a colon where the intended relation is unclear. The symbol B, presumably the branching fraction, is never defined.
   - The acronyms ggH, cH and SM are not defined. They are standard in this field.
   - Bullet 1 ends in a fragment ("clean H decay + a c-tagged jet"), and its last word "jet" wraps onto its own line.
   - "Flat direction" is in quotes and defined inline in bullet 4.
   - Bullet 3 points to the next talk (T. Bevilacqua) for flavour-scheme modelling.

3. **Figures.**
   - There are two LO Feynman diagrams for gc → cH and no data or simulation plots, so a CMS label and luminosity/energy do not apply.
   - Left diagram: an s-channel diagram. A gluon and a c quark merge into an internal c, which emits H and an outgoing c.
   - Right diagram: a t-channel diagram. The incoming c emits H, and the exchanged c line absorbs the gluon and becomes the outgoing c.
   - In both diagrams the Hcc̄ vertex is marked with a red dot labelled κc. This matches the caption, "LO diagrams for cH production; κc enters at the marked vertices".
   - The diagrams take up the lower half of the slide and are large enough to read when projected.
   - Nothing on the slide illustrates the g→cc̄ splitting background mentioned in bullet 3. The caption does not claim that it does.

4. **Layout.**
   - The reference line in the top right (small blue text) and the caption under the diagrams are in a smaller font than the bullets. They are readable but the smallest text on the slide.
   - Nothing overlaps or is clipped.
   - The κc labels are in red on a white background. Red is the only colour accent, and there is no red/green distinction.
   - The footer and page number (8/15) are at normal size.

content.reason: The message (κc enters at the production vertex in gc→cH, unlike H→cc̄) is in the title and bullet 1, and the two labelled LO diagrams support it. But it is buried in four wordy 2 to 3 line bullets with no take-away line. Bullet 2 is the key quantitative point, and its colon makes the relation unclear and B is undefined. The numbers are internally consistent (90 fb × B(γγ)≈0.23% ≈ 0.2 fb, × B(WW)≈21.5% ≈ 20 fb), but without the explicit ×B(H→X) form a pheno/ATLAS audience has to work this out. Bullet 3 brings up the g→cc̄ background and flavour scheme without anything on the slide showing them, and it hands the topic off to the next talk.

readability.reason: Nothing is clipped or overlapping. The diagrams are large in the lower half and the κc markers are clear (red on white, no red/green issue). Minor issues: the text block fills the top half and competes with the diagrams. The reference line and caption are the smallest text on the slide and only just comfortable from the back of the room. 'jet' wraps onto its own line in bullet 1.

issues.description: Bullet 2 'σcH = 90 fb: σB ≈ 0.2 fb (γγ), ≈ 20 fb (WW)': the colon hides the relation and B is undefined. The √s and the order of the 90 fb are also not stated.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite as 'σ(cH) ≈ 90 fb (SM, 13.6 TeV) → σ×B(H→γγ) ≈ 0.2 fb, σ×B(H→WW) ≈ 20 fb', with the √s/order matching the cited source.

issues.description: There is no take-away line. The slide does not say why cH matters relative to H→cc̄ (independent production-side handle, sign/flat-direction sensitivity).
issues.suggested_fix: Add a one-line boxed take-away at the bottom, e.g. 'cH: κc from production, complementary to H→cc̄ decay and breaks its flat direction'.

issues.description: The text is wordy: four bullets of 2 to 3 lines take up half the slide and compete with the diagrams.
issues.suggested_fix: Cut each bullet to one line. Drop or shorten the flavour-scheme bullet to 'Modelling (4FS vs 5FS): see next talk (T. Bevilacqua)'.

issues.description: Bullet 1 ends in a fragment, and 'jet' wraps alone onto a new line.
issues.suggested_fix: Rephrase to fit on one line, e.g. 'Signature: clean H decay + c-tagged jet'.

issues.description: The g→cc̄ splitting background in bullet 3 is mentioned but not shown, so it needs verbal explanation.
issues.suggested_fix: Either drop it from the slide (it is covered by the next talk) or add a small greyed diagram labelled 'background: g→cc̄ + H'.

issues.description: The reference line and caption are the smallest text on the slide.
issues.suggested_fix: Increase both by 2 to 4 pt, or shorten the caption to 'κc enters at the red vertices' so it can be larger.

9.description:
## Slide 9/15: cH(H→γγ)

**1. Message**
- The slide summarises the CMS cH(H→γγ) search, which sets a weak constraint on κc. The point is stated in a take-away line at the bottom: "|κc| ≲ 40, not ∼3: σB ≈ 0.2 fb, and ggH H+c mimics the signal". The image shows this line, but it is missing from the extracted text layer.
- A highlighted box gives the result: 95% CL obs. (exp.) µcH < 243 (355), |κc| < 38 (73).
- The source is cited at top right: JHEP 11 (2025) 060, CMS-HIG-23-010.

**2. Text**
- There are three bullets on the left, with two to three lines each. The amount of text is moderate.
- Symbols and acronyms used without definition on the slide: BDT, ggH, cH, µcH, κc, CL, S/(S+B), m_γγ. Some may have been defined on earlier slides.
- "9 categories per year (27 in total)" does not say which years. The 138 fb⁻¹ implies 2016 to 2018.
- The title "cH(H→γγ)" appears again as the header of the result box.
- The slide's own wording has no grammar problems. The plot legend contains the typo "S fit compoment", which comes from the published figure.

**3. Figures**
- There is one figure, the published CMS m_γγ distribution, with three stacked panels:
  - **Top panel:** S/(S+B)-weighted events / GeV against m_γγ, all categories. The labels "H→γγ, m_H = 125.38 GeV" and "µcH = −230 +170 −251" are inside the frame.
  - **Middle panel:** "Continuous background subtracted". It shows a peak near 125 GeV.
  - **Bottom panel:** "All background subtracted".
- The x-axis is m_γγ (GeV), from 100 to 180. The y-axis label carries units (/ GeV).
- Legend entries: Data, S fit component, S+B fit, All background, Continuous background, ±1σ (green), ±2σ (yellow).
- The figure carries a "CMS" label with 138 fb⁻¹ (13 TeV).
- The caption reads "m_γγ, all categories, weighted by S/(S+B)". It matches the plot.
- The figure takes up roughly a quarter of the slide width. Its tick labels, legend text and in-frame annotations are very small and probably not readable when projected.
- The take-away's numbers (σB ≈ 0.2 fb and the ggH H+c mimicking statement) are not shown in the plot or anywhere else on the slide. The |κc| ≲ 40 value matches the box (|κc| < 38).

**4. Layout**
- The bullets, result box and take-away line use readable font sizes. The plot's internal text is the only part that is too small.
- Nothing overlaps or is clipped.
- The result box uses grey text for the expected values (355, 73). This is lower contrast than the black observed values but still legible.
- The take-away line is in bold blue on white.
- The plot uses the standard green and yellow uncertainty bands. Its curves are told apart by colour and line style (red, magenta, black, dashed blue), so nothing depends on a red/green distinction alone.

content.reason: The message is clear: the cH(H→γγ) limit |κc| < 38 is weak. It is stated in a take-away line and backed by the result box. But the take-away's explanation (σB ≈ 0.2 fb, ggH H+c mimics the signal) has no support anywhere on the slide. Several symbols the outside audience needs are undefined (µcH, BDT, S/(S+B), ggH H+c). The fitted µcH = −230 shown in the plot is large and negative, it is not discussed, and the figure needs explaining that the slide does not give.

readability.reason: The bullets, result box and take-away are readable. The only figure, the three-panel m_γγ fit, takes about a quarter of the slide width, and its tick labels, legend and in-frame annotations (including µcH = −230) will not be readable when projected. So the figure is too small for its importance and its key content cannot be read. The take-away is also missing from the text layer, which matters for accessibility and for the PDF.

issues.description: The figure is about a quarter of the slide width, and its tick labels, legend and annotations (µcH = −230 +170 −251) will not be readable when projected.
issues.suggested_fix: Enlarge the plot to at least half the slide width, or show only the top or middle panel larger. Repeat the key number (best-fit µcH) in slide-size text next to it.

issues.description: The take-away's reasons (σB ≈ 0.2 fb, ggH H+c mimics the signal) are not supported anywhere on the slide.
issues.suggested_fix: Add one bullet with the SM σ×B for cH(γγ) and a short note that ggH with an extra c-jet is an irreducible background, citing the paper's table or figure. Otherwise remove the numbers from the take-away.

issues.description: Symbols the non-CMS audience needs are undefined: µcH, S/(S+B) weighting, BDT, ggH H+c.
issues.suggested_fix: Define µcH = σ/σ_SM for cH in the result box, and spell out 'BDT-based categories'. Add a short caption explaining that the S/(S+B) weighting is for display only.

issues.description: The best-fit µcH = −230 is large and negative but is not commented on, and theorists will ask about it.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a short note, e.g. 'best fit µcH = −230 +170 −251, compatible with the SM within ~1σ'.

issues.description: The take-away line is missing from the extracted text layer, so it may be an image or rendered in a way that is not real text.
issues.suggested_fix: Render the take-away as real text in the source (e.g. a beamer block or text box) so it shows up in the PDF text and in screen readers.

issues.description: '9 categories per year (27 in total)' does not say which years.
issues.suggested_fix: Write '9 categories × 3 years (2016–2018)'.

issues.description: The result box header repeats the slide title 'cH(H→γγ)'.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename the box header to e.g. '95% CL limits' or drop it.

issues.description: The expected values in grey have lower contrast than the observed values.
issues.suggested_fix: Use dark grey or black for the expected values and mark them with parentheses only.

issues.description: The published legend contains the typo 'S fit compoment'.
issues.suggested_fix: Leave it, since it is the official figure. Don't draw attention to it, and don't add a copy of it in your own text.
